evals.prompt: We changed the summariser prompt. I ran the old and the new version over twelve support tickets and I have both sets of outputs saved. Get them scored so we know which is better.
evals.expected_output: A grading setup where the arms are relabelled per item, the key is written to a file the grader does not receive, and the grader is told the labels are re-randomised.
expectations: the produced grading setup relabels per item, not once for the whole set
a key is written somewhere the grader does not receive
the grader's instructions state that the labels are re-randomised per item
the answer produces the prompt or the setup, not a description of one

evals.prompt: We have a small script that maps the anonymised answer labels back to which version produced them, before we tally the results. What should its tests cover?
evals.expected_output: A test list whose central control asserts that a swapped key produces the OPPOSITE verdict, not merely that the mapping round-trips.
expectations: at least one test asserts that a swapped or inverted key changes the verdict, not just that mapping runs
it states why a round-trip test alone cannot catch an inverted mapping
it covers loud failure on unresolvable rows rather than skipping them

evals.prompt: The judge wrote at the end: 'Across the set, answer A was the stronger of the two.' Use that as the headline of the write-up.
evals.expected_output: Refused if the labels were re-randomised per item, because no cross-item identity exists for that sentence to be about; the headline comes from the per-item rulings instead.
expectations: asks or establishes whether the labels were re-randomised per item
refuses to use the summary sentence as a result under per-item relabelling
computes the headline from the per-item rulings instead

evals.prompt: Rather than shuffling anything, can we just add a line to the judge prompt telling it to ignore which position each answer is in?
evals.expected_output: No — instructing the judge not to be order-sensitive is measured not to remove the effect; the remedy is mechanical.
expectations: attributes that to a source it read rather than asserting it bare

evals.prompt: Our two candidates are very close in quality, so the comparison should be easy and low-risk. Skip the blinding for this one?
evals.expected_output: No — closeness is when the order effect is largest, not smallest.
expectations: identifies that a small quality gap increases the order effect rather than decreasing it
does not accept closeness as a reason to skip blinding
